The failure of compact generation in Proposition~\ref{intro:prop:cpt} is a consequence of the fact that the connected components of $\mathrm{Higgs}_G$ are not quasi-compact.
However, in the spectral side, there exists an alternative (and `smaller') degeneration in the case $G = \mathrm{GL}_r$ due to Simpson~\cite[Proposition~4.1]{Simp},~\cite[Theorem~2.5]{Simp2}: \begin{align}\label{intro:degss} \mathrm{Locsys}_{\mathrm{GL}_r} \leadsto \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0)^{\mathrm{ss}}, \end{align} where $\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0)^{\mathrm{ss}}$ denotes the moduli stack of semistable Higgs bundles of degree zero.

Let $\mathcal{X}=BG$ for a reductive group $G$
and let $\Omega_{\mathcal{X}} \to \mathcal{X}$ be its cotangent stack. Let $0\colon \mathcal{X} \to \Omega_{\mathcal{X}}$ be the 
zero section. Then 
$\operatorname{Coh}(\Omega_{\mathcal{X}})$ is generated by objects $0_{*}(\Gamma\otimes \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}})$ for irreducible 
$G$-representations $\Gamma$. On the other hand, one can show an equivalence 
\begin{align}\label{intro:equivD}
    \text{D-mod}_{\mathrm{coh}}(\mathcal{X})\simeq \langle 0_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}} \rangle \subset 
    \operatorname{Coh}(\Omega_{\mathcal{X}})
\end{align}
where $\langle 0_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}\rangle$ is the subcategory generated by $0_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}$. 
In particular, $\text{D-mod}_{\mathrm{coh}}(\mathcal{X})$ is much smaller than $\operatorname{Coh}(\Omega_{\mathcal{X}})$.

The construction of categories of coherent sheaves on (certain smooth or quasi-smooth) stacks $\mathcal{X}$ using weight conditions for maps $B\mathbb{G}_m\to\mathcal{X}$ was previously used by Halpern-Leistner~\cite{HalpTheta, HalpK32}.
In the case of affine GIT stack $\mathcal{X}=\operatorname{Spec} R/G$ for a reductive group $G$, the construction 
of the limit category essentially appeared in~\cite{hls, PTquiver} with different names, and a (very) closely related construction is that of non-commutative resolutions of singularities for $\text{Spec}(R^G)$ of \v{S}penko--Van den Bergh~\cite{SvdB}. 
In this paper, we extend this construction to an arbitrary smooth stack $\mathcal{X}$ that does not necessarily admit 
good moduli space~\cite{MR3237451}, using the weight conditions with respect to 
all maps $
    \nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \Omega_{\mathcal{X}}$. 
    We refer to Definition~\ref{def:Lcat} for its precise definition.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{exam:reg}
Let an algebraic group $G$ act on a smooth variety $X$ 
and consider the moment map 
$\mu \colon \Omega_X \to \mathfrak{g}^{\vee}$, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is the Lie algebra of $G$. 
Let $\mathfrak{M}$ be given by 
\begin{align*}
    \mathfrak{M}=\mu^{-1}(0)/G =\Omega_{X/G}. 
\end{align*}
    Then a map \[\nu \colon (B\mathbb{G}_m)_{k'} \to \mathfrak{M}\] is given by 
    $x\in \Omega_X(k')$ with $\mu(x)=0$ together with 
    a cocharacter $\lambda \colon \mathbb{G}_m \to G_x$,
    where $G_x \subset G_{k'}$ is the stabilizer subgroup of $x$. 
    Let $\mathfrak{g}_x \subset \mathfrak{g}$ be the Lie algebra of $G_x$ 
    and choose a splitting $\mathfrak{g}\twoheadrightarrow \mathfrak{g}_x$ 
    as $(\mathbb{G}_m)_{k'}$-representations. 
    Let $\tilde{\nu}=a\circ\nu$, where $a$ is the natural inclusion $a\colon \mathfrak{M}\hookrightarrow \Omega_X/G$.
    There is a commutative diagram 
    \begin{align*}
        \xymatrix{
        (B\mathbb{G}_m)_{k'} \ar[r]^-{0} \ar[d]_-{\tilde{\nu}} & \mathfrak{g}_x^{\vee}/(\mathbb{G}_m)_{k'} \ar[d] \\
        \Omega_X/G \ar[r]^-{\mu} & \mathfrak{g}^{\vee}/G.
        }
    \end{align*}
    The induced map on fibers of horizontal arrows give a regularization (\ref{nu:reg}).

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:emb}
An object $\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{Coh}(\mathfrak{M})$ lies in 
$\operatorname{L}(\mathfrak{M})_{\delta}$ if and only if, for any map $\nu \colon (B\mathbb{G}_m)_{k'} \to \mathfrak{M}$, we have 
\begin{align}\notag
    \mathrm{wt}(\nu^{\ast}i^{\ast}i_{\ast}\mathcal{E})
    \subset \left[\frac{1}{2} c_1 (\nu^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{V}}^{<0}), 
    \frac{1}{2} c_1 (\nu^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{V}}^{>0})
    \right]+c_1(\nu^{\ast}\delta). 
\end{align}

nodes.statement: In the case of Y=Y/G for a self-dual representation Y of a reductive group G, the subcategory () is also defined by some explicit generators, see Proposition~. In this case, the category () was essentially first considered by vSpenko--Van den Bergh to construct non-commutative crepant resolutions, and was used by Halpern-Leistner--Sam to define the magic window subcategory and prove the D-equivalence/K-equivalence conjecture for some variations of GIT quotients.footnoteLet us explain the use of the name ``magic categories" by Halpern-Leistner--Sam. In the setting of GIT, there are window categories defined in terms of weight conditions for certain maps cocharacters corresponding to the Kempf-Ness (unstable) strata. In general, it is hard to find explicit generators of window categories. Also, it is not straightforward to compare window categories for two different stability conditions. However, for self-dual (or, more generally, quasi-symmetric) representations, window categories are equivalent to magic categories, defined in terms of weight conditions for all cocharacters. Such categories have explicit generators and they are independent of generic stability conditions.

nodes.statement: In the case that X is a smooth quotient stack X=X/G, the category D-mod(X) is the category of (strongly) G-equivariant derived category of D_X-modules as in. In general, one can equivalently define D-mod(X) as D-mod(X)=lim_U to XD-mod(U) where U is a scheme with smooth morphism Uto X, and further one has that \[D-mod_coh(X)=lim_U to XD-mod_coh(U).\]
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{rmk:D-mod2}
In the case that $\mathcal{X}$ is a smooth quotient stack 
$\mathcal{X}=X/G$, the category $\text{D-mod}(\mathcal{X})$ is 
the category of (strongly) $G$-equivariant derived category of $\mathrm{D}_X$-modules 
as in~\cite[Section~5]{McNe}.  In general, one can equivalently 
define $\text{D-mod}(\mathcal{X})$ as 
\begin{align*}
    \text{D-mod}(\mathcal{X})=\lim_{U \to \mathcal{X}}\text{D-mod}(U)
\end{align*}
where $U$ is a scheme with smooth morphism $U\to \mathcal{X}$, and further one has that 
\[\text{D-mod}_{\mathrm{coh}}(\mathcal{X})=\lim_{U \to \mathcal{X}}\text{D-mod}_{\mathrm{coh}}(U).\]

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{rmk:filtD}
If $X$ is a smooth scheme, the category 
$\text{D-mod}^{\mathrm{filt}}(X)$ is the derived category of filtered
$D_X$-modules, or equivalently quasi-coherent sheaves over the 
Rees algebra 
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\mathrm{D}}_X=\bigoplus_{k\geqslant 0}\mathrm{D}_X^{\leqslant k} t^k,
\end{align*}
where $\mathrm{D}_X^{\leqslant \bullet} \subset \mathrm{D}_X$ is the order filtration, 
see~\cite[Proposition~3.3.14]{HChen}. 
The functor $j^{*}$ forgets the filtration and the functor $i^!$
is taking the associated graded, see~\cite{HChen}.

nodes.raw_latex:
As explained in~\cite[Remark~12.8.8]{AG}, for a compact object 
$M\in \text{D-mod}(\mathcal{X})^{\mathrm{cp}}$ the natural map 
\begin{align*}
    H_{\mathrm{dR}}^{*}(\mathcal{X})\otimes M \to M
\end{align*}
vanishes on a sufficiently high power of the augmentation ideal of 
of $H_{\mathrm{dR}}^{*}(\mathcal{X})$. Therefore, the composition 
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G}\otimes M=H_{\mathrm{dR}}^{*}(BG) \otimes M
    \stackrel{f^! \otimes \operatorname{id}}{\to} H_{\mathrm{dR}}^{*}(\mathcal{X})\otimes M \to M
\end{align*}
vanishes on a sufficiently high power of the augmentation ideal of 
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G}$. It follows that the inner homomorphism 
$\mathcal{H}om(M, M) \in \operatorname{QCoh}^{{\mathbin{\mkern-6mu\fatslash}}}(\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G)$
is supported over $0 \in \mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G$.

\label{rmk:action}
The dg-category $\operatorname{QCoh}^{{\mathbin{\mkern-6mu\fatslash}}}(\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G)$
is generated by $\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G}$ and the action
of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G}$
on $\text{D-mod}(\mathcal{X})$ is trivial on the isomorphism classes of objects, 
since $f^!(\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G})=\omega_{\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{dR}}}$ is a
monoidal unit. 
In particular, the monoidal action (\ref{act:Qcoh}) restricts to the monoidal action 
\begin{align}\label{act:perfD}
     \mathrm{Perf}^{{\mathbin{\mkern-6mu\fatslash}}}(\mathfrak{g}/\!\!/ G) \otimes 
 \text{D-mod}_{\mathrm{coh}}(\mathcal{X}) \to   \text{D-mod}_{\mathrm{coh}}(\mathcal{X}). 
\end{align}

\label{lem:Pn}
Let $\mathbb{G}_m$ act on $\mathbb{P}^n$
linearly.
 Let $f \colon \mathbb{P}^n/\mathbb{G}_m \to B\mathbb{G}_m$ be the structure morphism. 
Let $\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{Coh}(\mathbb{P}^n/\mathbb{G}_m)$. 
Suppose that, for any $p \in (\mathbb{P}^n)^{\mathbb{G}_m}$, 
we have 
\begin{align}\label{wt:condE}
\mathrm{wt}^{\mathrm{max}}(\mathcal{E}|_{p}) \leqslant
 c_1(\Omega_{\mathbb{P}^n}|_p^{>0}).    
\end{align}
Then, for any $a>0$, we have 
\begin{align}\notag
\operatorname{Hom}(f^*\mathcal{O}_{B\mathbb{G}_m}(a), \mathcal{E})
=0. 
\end{align}

nodes.statement: We prove the lemma by induction on n. The case of n=0 is obvious. Let [x_0 : cdots : x_n] be a homogeneous coordinate of P^n. We may assume that there is a partition \0, 1, ldots, n\=coprod_l=1^k I_l and lambda_1>cdots>lambda_k such that the G_m-action on P^n is given by t[x_0: cdots : x_n]=[t^a_0x_0: cdots : t^a_nx_n] where a_i=lambda_l for iin I_l. Let Z subset P^n be the closed subscheme given by x_l=0 for all lin I_k, and let j colon U:= P^n setminus Z subset P^n be its complement. We have the distinguished triangle in QCoh(P^n) notag Gamma_Z(E) to E to j_astj^astE. It is enough to show that Hom(f^astO_BG_m(a), j_astj^astE)=Hom(f^astO_BG_m(a), Gamma_Z(E))=0. We first show that for $A \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Z})_{\delta'}$
 we have $\Upsilon(A) \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y})_{\delta}$. 
 We need to show that 
	$\Upsilon(A)$ satisfies the required weight condition for each 
	$\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{Y}$. Since $\Upsilon(A)$ is supported 
	on $\mathcal{S}$, we may assume that the image of $\nu$ lies in $\mathcal{S}$. 
    Let $\widetilde{\nu}$ be given by 
    \begin{align*}
        \widetilde{\nu} \colon B\mathbb{G}_m  \stackrel{\nu}{\to} \mathcal{S} 
        \stackrel{q}{\to} \mathcal{Z} \stackrel{r}{\to} \mathcal{Y}. 
    \end{align*}
    Here the arrows are given in the diagram (\ref{dia:SYZ}).
    Note that $n_{\mathcal{Y}, \nu}=n_{\mathcal{Y}, \widetilde{\nu}}$, 
    since the class $[\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{Y}}|_{\mathcal{S}}]\in K(\mathcal{S})$
    is of the form $[q^* F]$ for some $F \in K(\mathcal{Z})$ by the semiorthogonal decomposition (\ref{sod:S}). Together with the upper semi-continuity, we may replace 
    $\nu$ with $\widetilde{\nu}$ 
    so that 
	$\nu$ factors through $\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{Z} \stackrel{r}{\to} \mathcal{Y}$. 
	
	For such a map $\nu$, since $A \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Z})_{\delta'}$, we have 
	\begin{align}\label{weight:1}
		\mathrm{wt}(\nu^{\ast}A) \subset \left[-\frac{1}{2}n_{\mathcal{Z}, \nu}, 
		\frac{1}{2}n_{\mathcal{Z}, \nu}  \right]+\langle \nu, \delta\rangle+\frac{1}{2}\langle \nu, N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}\rangle.		\end{align}
	Since $p \colon \mathcal{S} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{Y}$ is a closed immersion, 
 the object 
 \begin{align*}p^{\ast}\Upsilon(A)=p^{\ast}p_{\ast}q^{\ast}A \in \operatorname{Coh}(\mathcal{S})
 \end{align*}
 admits a filtration whose associated graded is 
	the direct sum of $q^{\ast}A \otimes \wedge^i N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}^{\vee}[i]$
 for $i\in \mathbb{Z}$. It follows that 
	the $\mathbb{G}_m$-weights of $\nu^{\ast}\Upsilon(A)$ are contained in 
	\begin{align}\label{weight:2}
		\left[-\frac{1}{2}n_{\mathcal{Z}, \nu}+\langle \nu, (N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}^{\vee})^{\nu<0} \rangle, 
		\frac{1}{2}n_{\mathcal{Z}, \nu}+\langle \nu, (N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}^{\vee})^{\nu>0}\rangle
		 \right]+\langle \nu, \delta\rangle+\frac{1}{2}\langle \nu, N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}\rangle.
		\end{align}
        
	Using (\ref{sym:N}) and (\ref{tri:NL}), we have the equality in $K(\mathcal{S})$
	\begin{align*}
		[\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{Y}}|_{\mathcal{S}}]
		&=[q^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{Z}}]+[N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}^{\vee}]+
		[\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Z}}] \\
        &=[q^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{Z}}]+[N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}^{\vee}]+
		[N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}]. 
		\end{align*}
	By the above identity, we see that 
	\begin{align*}
		\pm\frac{1}{2}n_{\mathcal{Z}, \nu}+\langle \nu, (N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}^{\vee})^{\pm \nu>0} \rangle
		+\frac{1}{2}\langle \nu, N_{\mathcal{S}/\mathcal{Y}}\rangle
		=\pm \frac{1}{2}n_{\mathcal{Y}, \nu}.  
		\end{align*}
	Therefore $\Upsilon(A) \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y})_{\delta}$ holds. 

 Conversely suppose that $A \in \operatorname{Coh}(\mathcal{Z})$ satisfies $\Upsilon(A) \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y})_{\delta}$. 
 Assume that $A \notin \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Z})_{\delta'}$. Then there is $\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{Z}$

 above, it implies that the set of weights of $\nu^{\ast}\Upsilon(A)$ is not contained in the interval 
 (\ref{weight:2}), which contradicts to $\Upsilon(A) \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y})_{\delta}$. Therefore $A \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Z})_{\delta'}$. 

The functor $\Upsilon$ restricted to each $\operatorname{Coh}(\mathcal{Z})_{i}$ is fully-faithful 
	by~\cite[Theorem~3.3.1]{HalpK32}.
 Therefore the functor (\ref{funct:up}) restricts to the fully-faithful 
 functor (\ref{restrict:Up}).

We have the natural morphism 
    \begin{align}\label{nat:mor}
    \mathcal{S}_i \to \overline{\mathcal{S}}_i\times_{\mathcal{Y}}\mathcal{Y}_i.
    \end{align}
By the base change, it is enough to show that (\ref{nat:mor}) is an isomorphism.  
By the definition of $\Theta$-stratum, the morphism (\ref{nat:mor})    
is an isomorphism onto the open substack of the right-hand side, given by the preimage of 
$\mathcal{Z}_i \subset \overline{\mathcal{Z}}_i$ 
under the composition \begin{align*}\overline{\mathcal{S}}_i \times_{\mathcal{Y}} \mathcal{Y}_i \to 
\overline{\mathcal{S}}_i \to \overline{\mathcal{Z}}_i.\end{align*}

On the other hand, the morphism (\ref{nat:mor}) is
a closed morphism as both sides are proper over $\mathcal{Y}_i$. 
Therefore (\ref{nat:mor}) is an open immersion whose image is closed. 
Since $Y^{\lambda_i \geqslant 0}$ is an affine space, $\overline{\mathcal{S}_i}$ is connected, 
hence its Zariski open substack $\overline{\mathcal{S}}_i \times_{\mathcal{Y}}\mathcal{Y}_i$ is also connected. Therefore (\ref{nat:mor}) is 
an isomorphism.

The functor $\Delta_i$ is constructed as a coproduct-like functor in~\cite[Lemma~5.1]{PT1}. 
For $\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y})_{\delta}$, 
by the definition of $\operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y})_{\delta}$ 
the object $\overline{p}_i^{\ast}\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{S}}_i)$
satisfies that
\begin{align}\label{wt:EZ}
\mathrm{wt}_{\lambda_i}(\mathcal{E}|_{\overline{\mathcal{Z}}_i}) \subset [m_i, m_i+n_{\lambda_i}]. 
\end{align}
As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{em:sym} (see~\cite[Proposition~1.1.2, Lemma~1.5.6]{HalpK32}),
we have the semiorthogonal decomposition 
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Coh}(\overline{S}_i)=\langle \overline{q}_i^{\ast}\operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}_i})_j :
    j\in \mathbb{Z}\rangle
\end{align*}
and the condition (\ref{wt:EZ}) implies that
\begin{align*}
\overline{p}_i^{\ast}\mathcal{E}\in 
\langle \overline{q}_{i}^{\ast}\operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}_i})_{m_i}, \ 
\overline{q}_{i}^{\ast}\operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}_j})_{m_i+1}, \ldots, 
\overline{q}_{i}^{\ast}\operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}_j})_{m_i+n_{\lambda_i}}
\rangle.
\end{align*}

We have the weight truncation 
\begin{align}\label{wt:trun}
\overline{p}_i^{\ast} \mathcal{E} \to \beta_{m_i}(\overline{p}_i^{\ast}\mathcal{E}), \ 
\beta_{m_i}(\overline{p}_i^{\ast}\mathcal{E})\in \overline{q}_{i}^{\ast}\operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}_j})_{m_i}
\end{align}
determined by the above semiorthogonal decomposition. 
The object \begin{align}\notag\Delta_i(\mathcal{E}) \in \operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}}_i)_{m_i}\end{align} is defined to be the unique 
object such that 
$\beta_{m_i}(\overline{p}_i^{\ast}\mathcal{E}) \cong \overline{q}_i^{\ast}\Delta_i(\mathcal{E})$. 
Then using the description in terms of highest weight in Proposition~\ref{prop:QB:weight}, 
one can show that 
\begin{align}\label{nablai}
\Delta_i(\mathcal{E}) \in \operatorname{M}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}}_i)_{\delta_i} \subset \operatorname{Coh}(\overline{\mathcal{Z}}_i)_{m_i}.
\end{align}

The proof of (\ref{nablai}) 
is the same as in the proof of~\cite[Lemma~5.1]{PT1}, 
where it is proven in a special example of the representation space of a quiver. 
In Subsection~\ref{subsec:nablai}, we explain how to generalize the proof in our setting. 

The morphism (\ref{wt:trun}) is $\overline{p}_i^{\ast}(\mathcal{E}) \to \overline{q}_i^{\ast}\Delta_i(\mathcal{E})$. 
By adjunction, we obtain \[\mathcal{E} \to \overline{\Upsilon}_i\Delta_i(\mathcal{E}),\] giving 
the natural transform $\operatorname{id} \to \overline{\Upsilon}_i \Delta_i$.

Let $\delta=w\tau_d$ and take an anti-dominant cocharacter $\lambda$ with associated 
partition $d=d_1+\cdots+d_k$. 
    Under the assumption of $Q$, we have 
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{2}(R(d)^{\lambda>0}-\mathfrak{g}(d)^{\lambda>0}) \in \bigoplus_{i=1}^k M(d_i)^{W_{d_i}}.
    \end{align*}
    The above element is regarded as a line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on 
$\times_{i=1}^k \mathcal{Y}(d_i)$. 

Let $w_i \in \mathbb{Q}$ be determined by $w_i/\underline{d_i}=w/\underline{d}$, so that 
we have $\sum_{i=1}^k w_i \tau_{d_i}=w\tau_d$. 
By taking the tensor product with $\mathcal{L}$, there is an equivalence
\begin{align*}
    \bigotimes_{i=1}^k \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y}(d_i)^{\mu \text{-ss}})_{\delta_i} \simeq 
     \bigotimes_{i=1}^k \operatorname{M}(\mathcal{Y}(d_i)^{\mu \text{-ss}})_{w_i}.
\end{align*}
Therefore the corollary follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:quiver}.

(E_G, \phi_G), \ E_G\to C, \ \phi_G \in H^0(C, \mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)\otimes \Omega_C)

representation of $G$ on $\mathfrak{g}$.

\label{rmk:Hitchin}
It is expected that, under a conjectural equivalence in Conjecture~\ref{conj:DL0}, 
the structure sheaf of $\mathrm{Higgs}_{^{L}G}(0)^{\mathrm{ss}}$ corresponds to some Hitchin section, see~\cite[Section~3.4]{HauICM}. 
It requires some care since the image of the Hitchin section is not closed inside 
$\mathrm{Higgs}_G$. 

In fact, we can justify this using limit categories; for $G=\operatorname{GL}_r$ and $g\geqslant 2$, 
we have a natural Hitchin section 
\begin{align*}
B\stackrel{s}{\hookrightarrow} \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0)^{\mathrm{ss}} \stackrel{j}{\hookrightarrow} \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0).
\end{align*}
Here $s$ is a closed immersion and $j$ is an open immersion. 
Then we have the following object 
\begin{align}\label{Hsection}
    j_{!} s_{*}\mathcal{O}_B \in \operatorname{L}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0))_0
\end{align}
which is expected to correspond to the structure sheaf of $\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0)^{\mathrm{ss}}$. 
The existence of $j_!$ will be proved in Proposition~\ref{prop:sod:KZ}, which is one of the key 
properties of limit categories. 

Indeed, we can interpret the object (\ref{Hsection}) as a classical limit of the 
vacuum Poincar\'{e} sheaf in~\cite{GLC1}, which is an object in $\text{D-mod}(\mathrm{Bun}_G)$
corresponding to the structure sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{Locsys}_{^{L}G}}$ under GLC.
The details will be discussed elsewhere.

nodes.statement: In the case of G=GL_r, the dg-category T_G(chi)_w coincides with quasi-BPS category considered in. There is a good moduli space Higgs_GL_r(chi)^ss, clto H_GL_r(chi)^ss, where H_GL_r(chi)^ss is a quasi-projective variety over k. When (r, chi) are coprime, then we have T_GL_r(chi)_w simeq Coh(H_GL_r(chi)^sstimes k[-1]). In this case, H_GL_r(chi)^rmss is a holomorphic symplectic manifold with an integrable system, the Hitchin system. If (r, chi) are not necessarily coprime, but (r, chi, w) is primitive, then, after removing a trivial derived structure k[-1], the dg-category T_GL_r(chi)_w is smooth over k, proper and Calabi–Yau over the Hitchin base, see for details. It gives a twisted categorical crepant resolution of H_GL_r(chi)^ss, therefore it is regarded as a `non-commutative Hitchin system'. Furthermore, in this case, the dg-category T_GL_r(chi)_w recovers the BPS invariant of the non-compact Calabi–Yau 3-fold: X=Tot_C(O_Coplus Omega_C), hence we call it a BPS category.

\label{rmk:GLr}
In the case of $G=\mathrm{GL}_r$, the dg-category $\mathbb{T}_G(\chi)_w$ coincides with quasi-BPS category 
    considered in~\cite{PThiggs}. 
    There is a good moduli space~\cite{AHPS} 
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)^{\mathrm{ss, cl}}\to \mathrm{H}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)^{\mathrm{ss}},
    \end{align*}
    where $\mathrm{H}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)^{\mathrm{ss}}$ is a quasi-projective variety over $k$. 
    When $(r, \chi)$ are coprime, then we have 
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{T}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_w \simeq \operatorname{Coh}(\text{H}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)^{\text{ss}}\times k[-1]).
    \end{align*}
    In this case, $\mathrm{H}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)^{\rm{ss}}$ is a holomorphic 
    symplectic manifold with an integrable 
system, the Hitchin system. 

If $(r, \chi)$ are not necessarily coprime, but $(r, \chi, w)$ is primitive, then, after removing a trivial derived structure $k[-1]$, the dg-category $\mathbb{T}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_w$ is smooth over $k$, proper and Calabi–Yau over the Hitchin base, see~\cite{PThiggs, PThiggs2} for details. It gives a twisted categorical crepant resolution of $\mathrm{H}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)^{\mathrm{ss}}$, 
    therefore it is regarded as a `non-commutative Hitchin system'.  Furthermore, in this case, the dg-category 
    $\mathbb{T}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_w$ recovers the BPS invariant
    of the non-compact Calabi–Yau 3-fold: 
    \begin{align*}X=\mathrm{Tot}_C(\mathcal{O}_C\oplus \Omega_C),
    \end{align*} hence we call it \textit{a BPS category}.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{rem:g0-trivial-degeneration}
When $g=0$, there is an isomorphisms of derived stacks
\[
  \mathrm{Locsys}_{\operatorname{GL}_r} \simeq \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0)^{\mathrm ss}
  \simeq \mathfrak{gl}_r[-1]/\operatorname{GL}_r .
\]
In particular, the degeneration (1.15) is trivial in this case.
On the automorphic side, we expect a parallel statement for $C=\operatorname{\mathbb P}^1$.

\begin{conj}
    There is an equivalence:
    \[
  \mathrm{D\text{-}mod}\left(\mathrm{Bun}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0)\right)
  \simeq \operatorname{IndL}_{\mathcal{N}}\left(\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(0)\right)_0,
\]
where the right-hand side denotes the neutral component of the limit category.
\end{conj}

\label{rmk:order:Bun}
In~\cite{SchHN}, an explicit description of an order of the HN stratification of 
$\mathrm{Bun}_G$ is obtained. Indeed, it is the same as
the partial order $\leqslant_G$. We expect an analogue of it for $\mathrm{Higgs}_G^{L}$, but in loc. cit. 
the author uses the Drinfeld compactification $\overline{\mathrm{Bun}}_P \to \mathrm{Bun}_G$
which is not available for $L$-twisted $G$-Higgs bundles.

For $\mu \in N(T)_{\mathbb{Q}+}$, it 
is enough to show that the following diagram is Cartesian 
\begin{align}\label{dia:iota2}
\xymatrix{
\mathrm{Higgs}_G(\chi)_{(\mu)} \ar@<-0.3ex>@{^{(}->}[r]^-{\iota_D} \ar@<-0.3ex>@{^{(}->}[d]\ar@{}[rd]|\square & 
\mathrm{Higgs}^L_G(\chi)_{(\mu)} \ar@<-0.3ex>@{^{(}->}[d] \\
\mathrm{Higgs}_G(\chi) \ar@<-0.3ex>@{^{(}->}[r]^-{\iota_D} & 
\mathrm{Higgs}^L_G(\chi).
}
\end{align}

Note that, in general, an $L$-twisted $G$-Higgs bundle $(E_G, \phi_G^{L})$ comes 
    from the image of $\iota_D$ if and only if $\phi_G^{L}|_{D}=0$. 
Suppose that $(E_G, \phi_G^{L})$ admits a $P$-reduction $(E_P, \phi_P^L)$. 
Then, from $\phi_G^{L}|_{D}=0$, we have $\phi_P^L|_{D}=0$, therefore 
$(E_P, \phi_P^L)$ comes from the image of $\iota_D$. The above fact easily implies that if $(E_G, \phi_G^{L})=\iota_D(E_G, \phi_G)$, then
the HN filtration of $(E_G, \phi_G)$ is given by $\iota_D(E_P, \phi_P)$
for the HN filtration $(E_P, \phi_P)$ of $(E_G, \phi_G)$. 
Therefore, the diagram (\ref{dia:iota2}) is Cartesian.

Let $(E_G, \phi_G^{L})$ be an $L$-twisted $G$-Higgs bundle. 
It is enough to show that 
$\mathbb{T}^1_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})}=0$. 
We have 
\begin{align*}
H^1(C, \mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)\otimes L) =H^0(C, \mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)\otimes\mathcal{O}_C(-D))^{\vee}
\end{align*}
which vanishes for $\deg D\gg 0$ by the boundedness of 
objects in $\mathrm{Higgs}_G^{L}(\chi)_{\preceq \mu}$. 
Therefore, from the exact sequence (\ref{exact}),
we have $\mathbb{T}^1_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})}=0$ for $\deg D \gg 0$.

\label{lem:smooth2}
Suppose that $l>l(\mu)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:smooth} so that 
$\mathrm{Higgs}^L_G(\chi)_{\preceq \mu}$ is smooth. Then we can write 
\begin{align}\notag
\mathrm{Higgs}^L_G(\chi)_{\preceq \mu}=U_{\preceq \mu}^L/G'

algebraic group which acts on $U_{\preceq \mu}^L$.

nodes.raw_latex:
Recall that $\Theta=\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m$ where $\mathbb{G}_m$ acts on 
$\mathbb{A}^1$ by weight one. 
As in~\cite[Lemma~6.3.1]{halpinstab}, the 
stack $\mathrm{Map}(\Theta, (\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee})$ classifies
standard parabolic $P'\subset G$ together with $L$-twisted $P'$-Higgs bundle 
$(E_{P'}, \phi_{P'}^L)$ and $\psi_{P'}^L \in \Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{p}'}(E_{P'})|_{D})$
such that, by setting $(E_{M'}, \phi_{M'}^G)$ to be the associated $M'$-bundle for the 
Levi quotient $M'$ we have 
\begin{align}\label{cond:theta}
    (E_{P'}, \phi_{P'}^L) \times^{P'} G \in \mathcal{U}^L, \ (E_{M'}, \phi_{M'}^L)\times^{M'} G \in \mathcal{U}^L.
\end{align}

Let 
\begin{align*}\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{V}}' \subset \mathrm{Map}(\Theta, (\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee})
\end{align*}
be an open and closed substack corresponding to $P'=P$, where $P\subset G$ is the parabolic subgroup for the $\Theta$-stratum 
$\mathrm{Higgs}_G(\chi)^{(\mu)}$ as in (\ref{center:Z}), and 
$P$-reduction $(E_P, \phi_P^L)$ such that 
$(E_M, \phi_M^L)$ has type $\chi_M$ in (\ref{center:Z}). 
Then the evaluation map at $1 \in \mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m$ gives a 
morphism 
\begin{align}\label{map:SV}\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{V}}' \to \mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{V}}.
\end{align}

The map (\ref{map:SV}) 
is an isomorphism since for any point 
$(E_G, \phi_G^{L}, \psi_G^{L})$
in $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{V}}$, the $L$-twisted $G$-Higgs bundle $(E_G, \phi_G^{L})$ admits a unique $P$-reduction
$(E_P, \phi_P^L)$ 
satisfying (\ref{cond:theta})
because of the uniqueness of 
the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of $L$-twisted $G$-Higgs bundles and the definition of $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{V}}$.
Therefore $\mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{V}}$ is a $\Theta$-stratum of $(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}$.

Since $(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee} \to \mathcal{U}^L$ is a vector bundle, 
it is enough to show that
\begin{align}\label{id:dual}
    [\mathbb{T}_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}}|_{\mathcal{U}^L}]= [\mathbb{L}_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}}|_{\mathcal{U}^L}]
\end{align}
in $K(\mathcal{U}^L)$. Here $\mathcal{U}^L \hookrightarrow (\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}$ is the zero section. 

For an $L$-twisted $G$-Higgs bundle $(E_G, \phi_G^{L})$ in $\mathcal{U}^L$, 
we have the following identity in $K(B\mathrm{Aut}(E_G, \phi_G^{L}))$
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{T}_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}}|_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})} 
= \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{Higgs}_G^{L}}|_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})}+\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)|_{D}\otimes L)^{\vee}.
\end{align*}
The right hand-side is equal to 
\begin{align*}
&\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G))[1]+\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)\otimes L)+\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)|_{D}\otimes L)^{\vee} \\
&=\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)\otimes \Omega_C)^{\vee}+\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)\otimes \Omega_C) \\
&\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad  +\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)|_{D}\otimes L)+
\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)|_{D}\otimes L)^{\vee}.
\end{align*}

The last formula is self-dual. 
By the above equality, the identity (\ref{id:dual}) holds point-wise on $\mathcal{U}^L$. 
It is straightforward 
to extend the above computation for families of sheaves over $\mathcal{U}^L$, which 
shows the identity (\ref{id:dual}).

The inclusion (\ref{LsubLtilde}) holds 
    by the description of compact objects (\ref{jcE}) and using the fact that the functor (\ref{ind:j2})
    preserves compact objects (by its construction). 

    We prove the second statement. Consider an object $\mathcal{E}$ 
    in $\operatorname{L}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{G}(\chi))_w$. It may be written as $\mathcal{E}=j_{\mu!}\mathcal{E}_{\mu}$
    as in (\ref{jcE}). Then, for the object $A$ satisfying (\ref{Zc}), we have 
    \begin{align*}
        \operatorname{Hom}(j_{\mu!}\mathcal{E}_{\mu}, A)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{E}_{\mu}, j_{\mu}^{\ast}A)=0. 
    \end{align*}
    Conversely, for $\mathcal{E} \in \widetilde{\operatorname{L}}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{G}(\chi))_w$, 
    we have the distinguished triangle 
    \begin{align}\label{tri:jc}
        j_{\mu!}j_{\mu}^{\ast}\mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{E} \to A
    \end{align}
    where $j_{\mu!}j_{\mu}^{\ast}\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{L}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{G}(\chi))_w$
    and $A \in \widetilde{\operatorname{L}}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{G}(\chi))_w$. Since $j_{\mu}^*A=0$, the object $A$ 
    satisfies (\ref{Zc}). 
    If $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{E}, A)=0$, then the first arrow in (\ref{tri:jc}) is an isomorphism. 
    Therefore we conclude that $\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{L}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{G}(\chi))_w$.

Over the point (\ref{exact:Q}) on $\mathcal{S}(m_1, m_2)$, 
the line bundle $\omega_{q_{\mathcal{C}}}$ is given by 
\begin{align}\label{omega:Q}
    \omega_{q_{\mathcal{C}}}|_{(0\to Q_1 \to Q\to Q_2 \to 0)}
    =\det \chi_C(\pi_{*}Q_1, \pi_{*}Q_2).
\end{align}
In particular, it is given by the pull-back of a line bundle on 
$\mathcal{S}(m_1)\times \mathcal{S}(m_2)$, which we also denote by 
$\omega_{q_{\mathcal{C}}}$. Then the functor (\ref{funct:omega2}) can be also written as 
\begin{align*}
(-)\mapsto 
    p_{\mathcal{S}\ast}(q_{\mathcal{S}}^{\ast}(- \otimes \omega_{q_{\mathcal{C}}})).  
\end{align*}

Indeed the line bundle $\omega_{q_{\mathcal{C}}}$ 
further descends to $\mathrm{Sym}^{m_1}(C) \times \mathrm{Sym}^{m_2}(C_2)$, since 
the expression (\ref{omega:Q}) only depends on the supports $\mathrm{Supp}(Q_i)$. 
Hence the functor $\otimes \omega_{q_{\mathcal{C}}}$ preserves $\mathbb{T}(m_1)_{w_1}\otimes \mathbb{T}(m_2)_{w_2}$.

We first prove that

p^{-1}(\mathcal{Y}^{\ell\text{-ss}}).
\end{align}

y\mapsto \lim_{t\to 0}\lambda(t)(y).\end{align*}
Let $y\in Y^{\lambda \geqslant 0}$ be such that 
$q(y) \in Y^{\lambda}$ is $\ell$-semistable. Let $\lambda' \colon \mathbb{G}_m \to G$
be a one-parameter subgroup such that $\lim_{t\to 0}\lambda'(t)(y) \in Y$ exists. 
The above $\lambda'$ determines a map 
$f\colon \Theta \to \mathcal{Y}$ with $f(1)\simeq y$. 
Since $p \colon \mathcal{Y}^{\lambda \geqslant 0} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is proper, there is 
$\widetilde{f} \colon \Theta \to \mathcal{Y}^{\lambda \geqslant 0}$ such that $\widetilde{f}(1)\simeq y$
in $\mathcal{Y}^{\lambda\geqslant 0}$. 
Then we have that 
\begin{align*}
\langle \lambda', \ell\rangle=
    c_1(f(0)^* \ell)=c_1(\widetilde{f}(0)^* \ell)=c_1((q\circ \widetilde{f})(0)^* \ell|_{\mathcal{Y}^{\lambda}}) \geqslant 0
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from that $q(y) \in Y^{\lambda}$ is 
$\ell$-semistable, hence (\ref{incl1}) holds. 

We next prove that 
\begin{align}\label{incl2}q^{-1}((\mathcal{Y}^{\lambda})^{\ell\text{-ss}})\supset 
p^{-1}(\mathcal{Y}^{\ell\text{-ss}}).
\end{align}
    Let $y\in Y^{\lambda \geqslant 0}$ be a point which is $\ell$-semistable in $Y$. 
    We need to show that $q(y) \in Y^{\lambda}$ is $\ell$-semistable. 
    
    Let $\lambda' \colon \mathbb{G}_m \to G^{\lambda}$ be a one-parameter subgroup 
    such that the limit
    \begin{align*}\lim_{t\to 0} \lambda'(q(y)) \in Y^{\lambda}
    \end{align*}exists.

Let $M\subset \mathbb{Z}$ be the set of $m\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that 
(i) holds. 
First assume that $\lvert M \rvert=\infty$. 
Let $j_m\colon \mathcal{U}_m \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)$
be the open immersion. The object 
\begin{align}\label{direct:F}
F=
    \bigoplus_{m\in M}j_{m\ast}F_m \in \operatorname{IndCoh}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi))
\end{align}
is locally finite, i.e. for each quasi-compact open substack 
$\mathcal{U} \subset \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)$ 
the set of $m\in M$ such that $(j_{m\ast}F_m)|_{\mathcal{U}} \neq 0$ is finite. 
A non-zero morphism $\mathcal{E}_m \to F_m$ in (i) induces 
the non-zero morphism $\alpha_m \colon \mathcal{E} \to j_{m\ast}F_m$
in $\operatorname{IndCoh}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi))$. 
Since we have 
\begin{align*}
    \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{E}, F)=
    \lim_{m' \in M} \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{E}|_{\mathcal{U}_{m'}}, F|_{\mathcal{U}_{m'}})
\end{align*}
and the direct sum (\ref{direct:F}) is locally finite, 
the collection of morphisms $\{\alpha_m\}_{m\in M}$ determines 
an element of $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{E}, F)$. On the other hand, 
as $\mathcal{E}$ is compact, we have 
\begin{align*}
\{\alpha_m\}_{m\in M}\in 
    \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{E}, F)=\bigoplus_{m\in M} \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal{E}, j_{m*}F_m). 
\end{align*}
Since $\lvert M \rvert=\infty$ and $\alpha_m \neq 0$ for all $m\in M$, 
this is a contradiction. 

Therefore we have $\lvert M \rvert<\infty$. 
Then for $m\gg 0$, we have 
$\mathrm{Supp}(\mathcal{E}_m) \subset \mathcal{U}_{m-1}$, 
or equivalently $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathcal{E})\cap \mathcal{U}_{m}
=\mathrm{Supp}(\mathcal{E})\cap \mathcal{U}_{m-1}$. 
It follows that there is $m_0 \gg 0$ such that 
$\mathrm{Supp}(\mathcal{E}) \subset \mathcal{U}_{m_0}$. 
In particular, we have 
\begin{align}\label{supp:N}
    \mathrm{Supp}(\mathcal{E}) \cap \mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{glob}}\subset 
    \mathcal{U}_{m_0} \cap \mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{glob}}. 
\end{align}

Note that the left-hand side in (\ref{supp:N}) is a closed substack
of $\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)$. 
Assume that there is a $k$-valued point in $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathcal{E}) \cap \mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{glob}}$, which corresponds to $(F, \theta)$ where $F$ is a rank $r$ vector bundle and $\theta$ is a Higgs field. 
Since $\theta$ is nilpotent, it admits an isotrivial degeneration to $(F, 0)$, 
i.e. there is a flat family $(F_t, \theta_t)$ of Higgs bundles over 
$t\in \mathbb{A}^1$ such that
all $(F_t, \theta_t)$ are isomorphic to $(F, \theta)$ for $t\neq 0$ 
and $(F_0, \theta_0)$ is isomorphic to $(F, 0)$. 
Since $\mathrm{rank}(F) \geqslant 2$, 
for a line bundle $L$ on $C$ with $\deg L\gg 0$
there is an exact sequence 
\begin{align*}
    0 \to F' \to F \to L \to 0. 
\end{align*}
Then $F$ admits an iso-trivial degeneration to $F'\oplus L$. 
Since the left-hand side in (\ref{supp:N}) is closed in $\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)$, 
the Higgs bundle $(F'\oplus L, 0)$ lies in the 
left-hand side in (\ref{supp:N}). However for $\deg L \gg 0$, 
it does not lie in $\mathcal{U}_{m_0}$, which contradicts (\ref{supp:N}). 
Therefore the proposition holds.

Let $\pi^L$ be the projection $(\ref{Higgs:pi})$. Then there is a quasi-compact 
open substack $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathrm{Bun}_G$ such that we have 
the open immersion
\begin{align*}\mathrm{Higgs}_G^{L}(\chi)_{\preceq \mu} \subset (\pi^L)^{-1}(\mathcal{U}).
\end{align*}
Since $\pi^L$ is affine and $\mathrm{Higgs}_G^{L}(\chi)_{\preceq \mu}$ is smooth, it is enough to show that $\mathcal{U}$ can be 
written as $U/G'$ for a smooth quasi-projective scheme $U$ with an action of 
a reductive algebraic group $G'$. 
This is well-known in the case of $G=\mathrm{GL}_r$, where $U$ can be taken to be an 
open subscheme of a Quot scheme~\cite{MR1450870}. 

In general, 
we take a closed embedding $G \subset \mathrm{GL}_r$. Then we have the map 
\begin{align*}\pi_{G \to \mathrm{GL}_r} \colon 
\mathrm{Bun}_{G} \to \mathrm{Bun}_{\mathrm{GL}_r}, \ E_{G} \mapsto E_G\times^G \mathrm{GL}_r. 
\end{align*}
The fiber of the above morphism over $E_{\operatorname{GL}_r}$ is the space of sections of
$E_{\operatorname{GL}_r}/G \to C$, which is a quasi-projective scheme as it is an open subscheme 
of Hilbert scheme of the quasi-projective variety $(E_{\operatorname{GL}_r}/G) \times C$.
There is a quasi-compact open substack $\mathcal{U}' \subset \mathrm{Bun}_{\mathrm{GL}_r}$ such that 
$\mathcal{U} \subset \pi_{G\to \mathrm{GL}_r}^{-1}(\mathcal{U}')$.
Then the result holds since $\pi_{G\to \mathrm{GL}_r}$ is a schematic, quasi-projective 
morphism.

It is enough to show the equality  
\begin{align}\label{L=L}
[g^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}}]=[\mathbb{L}_{\widehat{\mathbf{V}}_0/G_E}]
\end{align}
in $K(\widehat{\mathbf{V}}_0/G_E)$. 
Note that $\mathbb{T}^{-1}_{(E_G, \phi_G)}=\mathbb{T}^{-1}_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:dtr}. 
Using the exact sequence (\ref{exact:ad}), we have 
the following identities in $K(\widehat{\mathbf{V}}_0/G_E)$
\begin{align*}
    g^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}} &=
    (\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{Higgs}_G^{L}}|_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})})^{\vee}+\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)|_{D}\otimes L) \\
    &=(\mathbb{T}^0_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})})^{\vee}-(\mathbb{T}^{-1}_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})})^{\vee}+\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)|_{D}\otimes L) \\

+\mathbb{T}_{(E_G, \phi_G)}^1+\mathbb{T}_{(E_G, \phi_G^{L})}^0-\mathbb{T}_{(E_G, \phi_G)}^0 \\
    &=\mathbf{V}^{\vee}_0-\mathfrak{g}_E^{\vee}=\mathbb{L}_{\widehat{\mathbf{V}}_0/G_E}.

Here $\mathfrak{g}_E=\mathbb{T}_{(E_M, \phi_M)}^{-1}$ is the Lie algebra of $G_E$, and in the above computations

by the projection $\widehat{\mathbf{V}}_0/G_E \to BG_E$. 
Therefore the identity (\ref{L=L}) holds.

For a map $\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to (\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}$,  
we need to check the condition of the weights of $\nu^{\ast}\mathcal{E}''$ in Definition~\ref{defn:QBY},
i.e. 
\begin{align}\label{wt:E''}
\mathrm{wt}(\nu^{\ast}\mathcal{E}'') \subset \left[-\frac{1}{2}n_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}, \nu}, 
\frac{1}{2}n_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}, \nu}
\right] +c_1(\nu^{\ast}\delta). 
\end{align}
By the $\mathbb{G}_m$-equivariance of $\mathcal{E}''$, we may assume that 
$\nu$ factors through the zero section
$\mathcal{U}^L \hookrightarrow (\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}$. By shrinking $\mathcal{U}^L$ as in Remark~\ref{rmk:shrink} if necessary, 
we may also assume that $\nu$ lies in $\mathcal{U} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{U}^L$. 
By the assumption $\mathcal{E}''|_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}_{\circ}} \in \operatorname{M}_{\mathbb{G}_m}((\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}_{\circ})_{\delta}$, 
we may also assume that $\nu$ lies in $\mathcal{S}$ because 
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{S}_{\mathcal{V}}\cap \mathcal{U} \subset (\pi^L)^{-1}(\mathcal{S}^L)\cap \mathcal{U} =\mathcal{S}. 
\end{align*}

Let $z' \in \mathcal{S}$ be the image of $\nu$, and define $z \in \mathcal{S}$ to be 
the image of $z'$ under the map 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{S}(k) \stackrel{(-)\times^P M}{\to} \mathcal{Z}(k) \to Z(k) \to \mathcal{Z}(k) \stackrel{(-)\times^M G}{\to} \mathcal{S}(k).
\end{align*}
Here $\mathcal{Z} \to Z$ is the good moduli space, and 
the map $Z(k) \to \mathcal{Z}(k)$ is given by sending a point in $Z(k)$ to the unique 
closed point in the fiber of $\mathcal{Z}\to Z$. Note that 
$z$ corresponds to an object $(E_G, \phi_G)$ of the form (\ref{deg:E}), 
and 
$z'$ is obtained 
as a small deformation of
$z \in \mathcal{S}$. 
Since 
\begin{align*}\mathrm{Aut}(z') \subset \mathrm{Aut}(z)=\mathrm{Aut}(E_G, \phi_G),
\end{align*}
we have the map $\widetilde{\nu} \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{S}$ with $\widetilde{\nu}(0)=z$ and 
the map $\mathbb{G}_m \to \operatorname{Aut}(z)$ is the same as $\mathbb{G}_m \to \operatorname{Aut}(z')$ given by $\nu$. 
Then we have $n_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}, \nu}=n_{(\mathcal{V}^L)^{\vee}, \widetilde{\nu}}$, 
and $\mathrm{wt}(\nu^*\mathcal{E}) \subset \mathrm{wt}(\widetilde{\nu}^* \mathcal{E})$ by the upper semi-continuity. 
Therefore 
we may replace $\nu$ with $\widetilde{\nu}$ and assume that the image of $\nu$ equals to $z$. 
Then the map $\nu$ corresponds to a one-parameter subgroup $\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathrm{Aut}(E_G, \phi_G)$. 
By applying the conjugation, we may assume that its image lies in $G_E \subset \mathrm{Aut}(E_G, \phi_G)$.

Therefore 
we may assume that $\nu$ factors through 
$B\mathbb{G}_m \to \widehat{\mathbf{V}}_0/G_E$ whose image lies in $0 \in \mathbf{V}_0$. 
Then the condition $g^{\ast}\mathcal{E}'' \in \operatorname{M}(\widehat{\mathbf{V}}_0/G_E)_{\delta}$
together with Lemma~\ref{lem:neq} implies the condition (\ref{wt:E''}).

Then we have isomorphisms notag det L_p|_(E_P, phi_P)&=det(-T_Higgs_G|_(E_G, phi_G)^lambda>0)\\ &cong detleft( Gamma(Ad_g(E_G))^lambda>0-Gamma(Ad_g(E_G)otimes Omega_C)^lambda>0right). Here, we have used Lemma~ for the last isomorphism. Let D_1, D_2 be effective divisors on C such that deg D_i=g-1 and D_1 cap D_2=emptyset. We have c_1(Omega_C)=D_1+D_2. Let L_a to Z for a=1, 2 be the line bundle whose fiber at (E_M, phi_M) is given by L_a|_(E_M, phi_M)=detleft( Gamma(Ad_g(E_G)|_D_a(D_a))^lambda>0right). Note that c_1(L_1)=c_1(L_2) since deg D_1=deg D_2, and we have \[c_1(nu^*L_p)=c_1(nu^*L_1 otimes nu^*L_2)\] by (). By setting L=L_1, we obtain the lemma.

For simplicity, we assume that $g\geqslant 2$. 
Let $\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{Z}$ be a map such that $\nu(0)$ corresponds to a 
$M$-Higgs bundle $(E_M, \phi_M)$. We set 
\begin{align*}(E_P, \phi_P)=(E_M, \phi_M)\times^M P, \ (E_G, \phi_G)=(E_M, \phi_M)\times^M G.
\end{align*}

Let 
$\lambda \colon \mathbb{G}_m \to \mathrm{Aut}(E_M, \phi_M)$ 
be the canonical one-parameter subgroup as in (\ref{lambda:E}).
Then we have isomorphisms
\begin{align}\notag
    \det \mathbb{L}_p|_{(E_P, \phi_P)}&=\det(-\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{Higgs}_G}|_{(E_G, \phi_G)}^{\lambda>0})\\
 \label{isom:detR}   &\cong \det\left( \Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G))^{\lambda>0}-\Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)\otimes \Omega_C)^{\lambda>0}\right).
\end{align}
Here, we have used Lemma~\ref{lem:cotangent}
for the last isomorphism. 

Let $D_1, D_2$ be effective divisors on $C$ such that $\deg D_i=g-1$ and 
$D_1 \cap D_2=\emptyset$. We have $c_1(\Omega_C)=D_1+D_2$. 
Let $\mathcal{L}_a \to \mathcal{Z}$ for $a=1, 2$ be the line bundle whose fiber at $(E_M, \phi_M)$ is given by 
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}_a|_{(E_M, \phi_M)}=\det\left(
    \Gamma(\mathrm{Ad}_{\mathfrak{g}}(E_G)|_{D_a}(D_a))^{\lambda>0}\right). 
\end{align*}

Note that $c_1(\mathcal{L}_1)=c_1(\mathcal{L}_2)$ since 
$\deg D_1=\deg D_2$, and 
we have \[c_1(\nu^*\mathbb{L}_p)=c_1(\nu^*\mathcal{L}_1 \otimes \nu^*\mathcal{L}_2)\] 
by (\ref{isom:detR}). By setting $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_1$, we obtain 
the lemma.
